decisions.summary: Rack-by-the-house knob is HamletSpec.harvest_weather (settled|changeable), declared, never rolled; default settled; entry 500's knob folded in.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-005: the research found the environment decided, so the knob is set from a stated environment input; the GM's own worry was neighboring villages in one microclimate differing.

decisions.summary: Sawada declares harvest_weather=changeable as the pool's exhibit.
6 x 3 ft mats in rows, 1 ft edge clearance, gaps 2/1.5/1 ft never below 1 ft, hand-laid nudge and turn kept only where clear of neighbors; count in [ceil(full/3), floor(2 full/3)], thinned evenly.
decisions.why: Unchanged; the GM's 'render a bunch of mats over the yard', 'a smaller number to give the impression that there are many', 'three to six foot mats size to the yard'.

decisions.summary: The nudge and turn salted per yard.
decisions.why: Unchanged; a degree of the hand-laid convention.

decisions.summary: Of equal counts, the lattice whose seated mats' box sits nearest the yard's center.
decisions.why: Unchanged; a placement choice among layouts seating the same number.

decisions.summary: A yard that physically cannot hold a third at a 1 ft gap draws as many as fit at it, at any size.
decisions.why: As ruled in round 5: the third is this project's proxy for the GM's aim, and forcing it on a yard that cannot hold it at 1 ft draws paving, defeating the aim that the mats read as mats.

decisions.summary: 'Cannot reach a third at 1 ft' decided by the quarter-foot search, then, before a yard is let off, an exact solve: every crossing of two fit-condition lines on the lattice origin, each seated set confirmed at its group's centroid and, where the rack cuts a region into an L, a hair to each side of every crossing.
decisions.why: Round 9's objection (the down direction sampled at 0.02 ft) is gone: the solve has no step in either direction, and the L-region aside is closed (MAT_PROBE_FT, pinned by the 10 x 7 ft test). On this round's own run (a scratch test via make test-file, 2026-09-28, 834 s): 160 random yards 12-40 ft wide at h/w 0.6-0.75, corners pulled in up to 0.8 ft, a third with a rack from rack_segment at a random rake, a third with an arbitrary keep-out box, compared against a brute grid over every origin at 0.05 ft with a random anchor and strict fit - the brute never seated more than _exact_lattice. So 'cannot hold a third' now means the geometry cannot, which is the exception as ruled.

decisions.summary: SC-001's pool test runs an oracle on a 0.02 ft grid anchored 0.01 ft off on every short pool yard's outline and rack, and a test shows it sees the old counts.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-004's floor as the spec states it; not scope.

decisions.summary: The short-yard floor is four mats.
decisions.why: Bounds the exception; FR-004 as accepted.

decisions.summary: Rack along a side edge inset 1 ft, near half preferred, off the yard's map-south half solved in map coordinates, whole-side fallback; 2.5 ft drawn width a convention; mats skip its footprint; manifest gains mats and rack.
decisions.why: Unchanged. FR-006 and the GM's 'they should not be at the south side of the yard'.

decisions.summary: Threshing yard docstring rewritten from 025 and 505 with labels and the GM's convention wording.
decisions.why: FR-007; the GM's 'the pop-up should explain'.

decisions.summary: Regenerate the five pool hamlets; the settlement-reviews the gate owes; make done.
